newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sets up permanent human rights commission.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sets up permanent human rights commission.

text.p: Sri Lanka has set up a permanant human rights commission with broad monitoring and investigative powers, a government minister said on Monday.
Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris said the five-member body would replace the existing human rights task force to rectify inadequacies in existing rights laws.

The commission will try to settle disputes before they go to court, advise the government on flaws in existing human rights protections laws and raise community awareness of rights issues, Peiris said.
"The setting up of this Human Rights Commission is an historic occasion," Peiris told a news conference. "The protection of human rights is one of the most fundamental concerns of our government."

Sri Lanka has been accused of widespread human rights abuses with rights groups saying that up to 60,000 people died or disappeared during a brutal government crackdown on a leftwing youth insurgency in 1988-90.
Government forces fighting the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in the island's north and east have also been accused of violations.
